record.original_question: For a given class of optimization problems, how should the parameters of a nature-inspired algorithm be tuned so that the algorithm achieves its best performance, and how should those parameters be varied or controlled during the run to maximize performance?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. How to best tune the parameters of a given algorithm so that it can achieve its best performance for a given set of problems? How to vary or control these parameters so as to maximize the performance of an algorithm?

artifact.category_tag: parameter tuning and control in metaheuristics
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a nature-inspired (meta)heuristic optimization algorithm depending on a finite vector of control parameters θ ∈ Θ ⊆ R^k (for example, population size, mutation/crossover rates, inertia weights, cooling schedules, etc.). Let F be a specified class of optimization problems f : D → R (with D a given search domain), and let P(A, θ, f, t) denote a chosen scalar performance measure of A applied to problem f with parameters θ over a computational budget t (for instance, expected best-so-far objective value, success rate of reaching an ε-optimum, or expected runtime to a target).

(a) Static tuning. Determine, for the class F, a parameter setting
   θ* ∈ arg max_{θ ∈ Θ}  E_{f ∼ F} [ P(A, θ, f, t) ],
and provide a constructive, theoretically justified procedure for finding θ* (or a provably near-optimal surrogate) that does not rely solely on exhaustive empirical search.

(b) Dynamic control. Allow the parameters to be a function θ(s) of the algorithm's internal state s (iteration counter, population statistics, search history, etc.). Determine a control policy
   π* : S → Θ
that maximizes E_{f ∼ F} [ P(A, π, f, t) ] over admissible policies π, and characterize structural properties (monotonicity, schedules, feedback rules) of optimal or near-optimal policies for natural classes F.

Provide either explicit optimal/near-optimal tuning rules and control policies for meaningful classes F, or rigorous performance guarantees (upper and lower bounds) for the resulting tuned algorithm.
artifact.status_search_result: Parameter tuning and on-line parameter control of nature-inspired/evolutionary algorithms is a long-standing open research area. Surveys (e.g., Eiben & Smit; Karafotias, Hoogendoorn & Eiben; Huang, Li & Yao 2020) explicitly describe it as unsolved in general, with only partial theoretical results for specific algorithms (e.g., optimal mutation rates for (1+1) EA on OneMax, self-adjusting schemes with provable guarantees). No general solution exists.

status_evidence.title: Automated Algorithm Configuration and Parameter Tuning
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys note parameter tuning remains an open challenge with no universal solution, only domain-specific heuristics and partial theory.
status_evidence.claim: General parameter tuning and control of metaheuristics is recognized as an open research problem.

status_evidence.title: Parameter Control in Evolutionary Algorithms: Trends and Challenges
status_evidence.snippet: Karafotias et al. survey existing parameter-control methods and conclude that principled, generally applicable techniques are still lacking.
status_evidence.claim: Dynamic parameter control lacks a general theoretical framework.
